claims.text: The initial microstructure consists of dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries.
Optimizing lamellar colony size through hierarchical microstructure design will reduce microcrack initiation.
Optimizing boundary density through hierarchical microstructure design will reduce microcrack initiation.
The hierarchical microstructure will promote more homogeneous deformation.
Reduced microcrack initiation and more homogeneous deformation will increase tensile strength.
Reduced microcrack initiation and more homogeneous deformation will increase room-temperature tensile ductility.
The designed microstructure will have greater strength than the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The designed microstructure will have greater room-temperature tensile ductility than the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The relationship among lamellar colony size, boundary density, and mechanical properties is not well established.
The optimal lamellar colony size and boundary density are uncertain.
